name: Jiribam Town
description: Western gateway and municipal town of Manipur on the Jiri River border with Assam, serving as the state's sole railhead and a cultural crossroads of Meitei and plains communities.
facts: Headquarters of Jiribam district, created 2016 from Imphal East

name: Ningshingkhul Biodiversity Park
description: Official biodiversity park featuring aquatic and terrestrial plants and animals, with Ancestral Heroes Complex for homage, ideal for nature education and recreation near the town.
facts: About 6 km from Jiribam Bazar and railway station
Official tourist place listed by district administration

name: Jiribam Railway Station
description: First railway station in Manipur, opened in 1903, serving as the railhead on the Silchar-Jiribam line and key connectivity point for the western border region.
facts: Station code JRBM, Northeast Frontier Railway

name: Statue of Lamyanba Hijam Irabot
description: Memorial statue of Jana Neta Hijam Irabot (1896-1951) in Irabot Square/Babupara, commemorating the socio-political leader and freedom movement figure of Manipur.
facts: Focal point for annual observances on birth and death anniversaries

name: Nongshaba Gate (Nongsaba Sanathong)
description: Western Gate of Manipur, a symbolic entrance structure inaugurated as a landmark for the state's western boundary and cultural identity.
facts: Inaugurated by Chief Minister as western gateway symbol

name: Jiri River
description: Border river defining the western edge of Jiribam and Manipur, offering scenic banks for boating, fishing, and views of the valley and agricultural plains.
facts: Confluence area with Barak River near Jirimukh

name: Barak River (Jiribam section)
description: Major river flowing through the Jiribam valley, supporting the region's plains, agriculture, and scenic landscapes near the Assam border.
facts: Turns west near Jirimukh south of Jiribam

name: Sahab Uddin Agor Garden
description: Specialized garden focused on agarwood (Aquilaria) cultivation, serving as a unique agri-tourism and botanical site in the Jiribam area.
